chunks.title: Model game creation and time controls
acceptance_criteria: New games accept untimed play, required presets, or validated custom base and increment values
White and Black labels receive sensible defaults and participant types are stored without changing rules behavior
Game creation initializes canonical board, lifecycle, clock, ownership, and persistence state consistently
Focused tests cover valid presets/custom games and malformed or out-of-range inputs

chunks.title: Implement server-authoritative clocks
acceptance_criteria: Clock calculations use server timestamps, persisted remaining time, active color, and increment rather than browser intervals
Accepted moves debit elapsed time and apply increment exactly once while rejected moves do neither
Refreshing or reloading a game cannot pause, reset, or double-debit the active clock
Tests use an injected deterministic clock and cover both colors, increments, refresh, and boundary timing

chunks.title: Add complete game-ending actions
acceptance_criteria: Resignation, accepted draw offers, valid draw claims, abandonment, and timeout set canonical result and termination fields
Timeout records a draw when the opponent cannot legally win and a loss otherwise
Finished games reject moves, actions, and clock mutations without changing saved state
Focused positive and negative tests cover authorization, action ordering, and every termination path

chunks.title: Persist transitions and expose history replay services
acceptance_criteria: Every accepted owned-game move or lifecycle transition is saved atomically with clock and terminal metadata
Personal history lists required date, result, labels, time control, and completion reason fields for only the active owner
Opening a saved game returns canonical final state and ordered immutable replay positions
Stepping through replay data cannot mutate the saved game or active session game

chunks.title: Publish lifecycle history and replay APIs
acceptance_criteria: HTTP contracts cover new game, move, resign, draw offer/accept/claim, abandon, history, saved-game open, and replay data
Controllers enforce method, input, authentication, and ownership boundaries with stable JSON envelopes
Generated API documentation describes clock, participant, lifecycle, history, and replay state
Integration tests cover representative untimed and timed API journeys including persistence across sessions
